headline: Five days to the crossing. The taper has held clean and the final travel window is here. Everything from now is logistics — the trail writes the rest.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture in this last week before departure is exactly what a deliberate wind-down should look like: short, easy runs sitting almost entirely low, one of them faster on tired-free legs and one distinctly conversational, with no attempt to chase load. Strength has gone quiet in the final week, which is appropriate — the durability work banked over the prior weeks doesn't evaporate in a few rest days, and lifting hard now would only add fatigue with no upside. Steps remain genuinely high, which matters more than it looks: it means the taper is a running taper, not a movement taper, so residual mobility and time-on-feet conditioning stay live right up to the transition. The cardio-load status reading itself flags detraining, but that's a mechanical artefact of a deliberate quiet stretch, not a fitness signal — it's the plan reporting itself back. The one thread that's stayed genuinely variable, rather than deliberately quiet, is recovery.
sections.trends: Zoomed out, the year-to-date shape is unambiguous — this year's accumulated distance dwarfs the same point last year, and the recent four-week block was up meaningfully on the prior one before this final taper. That's a base that's been built patiently and then intentionally stepped down, not a plateau or a stall. The current dip in running load is the last, smallest step of that deliberate descent, and reading it as anything other than an intentional pre-event drawdown would misread the whole arc that led here.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and the aerobic markers have held flat across the baseline window, which at this stage is precisely what you want — the engine has been maintained, not sharpened or eroded, going into an event where sustained low-intensity durability over many days matters far more than a sharpened top-end. There's no signal of aerobic decline; the flatness is stability, and stability is the right state to arrive in.
sections.zones: The per-session shapes over the taper tell the story cleanly: the recent runs sit overwhelmingly in the lowest zones, with the faster short effort still capped well below any real cardiovascular cost, and the last genuine intensity — the long, hard mid-July session with substantial Z3 and Z4 time — sits far enough back to be fully absorbed. That's a textbook taper distribution: intensity earned early, then a controlled, low-grey-zone glide into the start. Nothing in the recent sessions contradicts the intent.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength HR has been consistent with easy, low-zone functional work rather than metabolically taxing lifting — sitting low with brief excursions upward, which fits maintenance-style sessions. Nothing in the source agreement stands out as worth flagging; the run and strength HR patterns read coherently across the block.
sections.calendar: The frequency pattern this week is the signature of a taper done properly — runs kept frequent but short, so movement rhythm and neuromuscular familiarity stay intact even as volume drops. That's smarter than going dark entirely before a long effort; the body stays primed to move daily, which is exactly the state a 9-10 day self-supported push demands from day one.
sections.personal_bests: No PBs are in play here and none should be — the training focus has correctly shifted entirely toward arriving fresh and durable for a multi-day effort. The existing speed bests are bankable capacity for later in the year; they're not the point of this window and won't be touched by a taper.

watch_items: Watch whether recovery nights finally steady through the travel-and-transition days — it's been the one persistently variable thread and the one that compounds most once daily pack-loaded efforts stack up.
Over the opening stretch, note how "easy" HR responds as consecutive loaded days accumulate — the first few days will redefine what easy actually costs.
Track the back-to-back leg response early; cumulative durability under a 6-8kg pack is the genuine unknown, not the underlying engine.
Once the trail begins, watch how the mountain-crossing section sits within the daily rhythm — the border climb is the one terrain spike worth reading separately from the flatter days.
